correctness.rationale: Re-audit of the repaired theorem: the source stationary density/current data apply to the thermodynamic active Gibbs state and give an increasing density coordinate, zero currents at its endpoints and one positive stationary root by the derivative factorization and Descartes' rule. With ε=q^−1/3 and c=2^(1/3), the scaled stationarity polynomial has a simple positive zero at c when ε=0 and linear term −2εv³, giving v*=c+c²ε/3+O(ε²). The expansion of j at s=εv is 1−ε(v+v^−2)+ε²(v²+v^−4)+O(ε³); the derivative of the first-order deficit vanishes at c. The density identity gives 1−ρ*=(c/2)ε−(c²/12)ε²+O(ε³). Independently, the Markov transition odds imply (q−1)x²+x=ρ(1−ρ) for the nearest-neighbor 10 probability x. Therefore the subleading eigenvalue is R=(D−1)/(D+1), with D²=1+4(q−1)ρ(1−ρ), and the infinite susceptibility is ρ(1−ρ)D. Along the optimum D=c²/ε−2/3+O(ε), and ξ=D/2+O(1/D), giving the additive −1/3. Multiplication by ρ*(1−ρ*)=(c/2)ε−(c²/3)ε²+O(ε³) gives 1−cε+O(ε²). At fixed density the same formula gives √(qρ(1−ρ)); the repaired text compares explicitly to Eq. (19) without attributing the printed error to a conjectured omission. These are analytic checks; the source check script was inspected, not run.
